headline: High risk of data leakage and cascading errors: RD-Agent’s broad egress plus Replit Agent’s writable Repl workspace can expose sensitive research/code and propagate unchecked outputs.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: RD-Agent can run browsers and ingest web content, while Replit Agent reads/writes the Repl workspace. A shared workspace or copied outputs create a plausible instruction-injection path, but no direct shared channel is documented here, so I avoid high.
conditions: IF RD-Agent writes browser-sourced text into a Repl workspace file that Replit Agent later parses as instructions
IF the two agents are connected by copy-paste or a shared file mount
mitigations: Keep agent outputs in separate directories
Require explicit human review before Replit Agent executes text from RD-Agent
Strip instructions from scraped web content before saving
Use read-only handoff files
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to inter-agent files

B_data_leakage.rationale: RD-Agent touches financial reports, competition datasets, logs, and has broad network egress; Replit Agent touches source code, secrets, and deployment config and also has broad egress. If they share a workspace or secrets, either can expose sensitive data externally, and the blast radius includes secrets and research artifacts.
conditions: IF both agents access the same workspace or secret store
IF either agent sends workspace contents to external APIs during normal operation
mitigations: Separate secrets stores per agent
Disable network egress for one agent during sensitive tasks
Use distinct workspaces
Rotate any exposed API keys
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention rules

C_capability_conflict.rationale: RD-Agent supports multiple instances and Replit Agent can write the filesystem and modify git state. If both operate on the same repo or Repl, concurrent writes can corrupt code or commits; uncertainty is limited because both write-capable surfaces are explicit.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same repository or Repl filesystem
IF git operations occur without locking or branch isolation
mitigations: Assign separate branches
Pause one agent during the other's write phase
Use file locks for shared paths
Review git diffs before merge
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: RD-Agent produces research outputs and logs, and Replit Agent can act on workspace contents with shell and package installation. That makes it plausible for Replit Agent to treat RD-Agent outputs as authoritative without verification, but the profiles do not show an explicit auto-execution chain, so medium fits.
conditions: IF Replit Agent consumes RD-Agent-generated files as ground truth
IF those files trigger shell commands, package installs, or code changes without review
mitigations: Require a verification step before acting on RD-Agent outputs
Mark RD-Agent artifacts as untrusted by default
Limit Replit Agent to read-only review mode for handoffs
Compare outputs against source data
requires-engineering: add schema validation for handoff files

E_compliance.rationale: RD-Agent explicitly handles financial reports and competition datasets, while Replit Agent handles secrets and deployment configuration in a cloud Repl. The profiles do not specify residency or retention controls, so a compliance mismatch is plausible but not proven; uncertainty pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF regulated financial or personal data is placed into the Replit workspace
IF retention or residency requirements apply to data processed by either agent
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the Replit workspace
Document data residency for both agents
Use synthetic or redacted datasets
Review retention settings before use
requires-engineering: add compliance gating for sensitive datasets
